newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares dip on conflicting poll rumours.
newsitem.headline: French shares dip on conflicting poll rumours.

text.p: The French share market closed lower on Thursday, buffeted by rumours of conflicting private opinion polls on Sunday's election runoff, while a spat over Bundesbank gold drew attention away from domestic events, dealers said.

The share market has fallen more than six percent over the last four days as investors take more seriously the prospect of a left-wing win in the election. It stabilised on Thursday as dealers decided Wednesday's losses were excessive.
"I do not even try to understand anymore, there are really no targets either up or down, it's purely reacting to rumours," a broker said.

Thursday's morning rise was underpinned by a rumour, later proved without foundation, of an opinion poll putting right-wing parties in a strong position while a series of other rumoured private polls said the left was well placed.
The publication of opinion polls was banned in France from one week before last Sunday's first round, in which the left scored an unexpected win over the ruling centre-right coalition.
Three polls were published on a California-based internet site and a fourth was released by a Swiss-based French language newspaper on Thursday evening.
Brokers said the market was getting more and more convinced that the left-wing could win the second-round of the election on Sunday.
"It's a market of excesses. There have been enormous swings but they do not mean much. On top of that, the dollar is up and the international situation is not bad," a broker said.
The dollar was boosted by a flow of funds out of the mark in the wake of a spat between the Bundesbank and the Bonn government over the revaluation of Bundesbank gold.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed 0.15 percent lower at 2579.24. It hit a high of 2,627.54 and a low of 2,566.92. Volume was a very brisk 10.69 billion francs after having reached a total of 12.45 billion francs for one of the highest daily turnover figures on Wednesday.
The index closed at 2,522.67 on Monday April 21 before President Jacques Chirac called the snap election.
French bond futures erased earlier losses to settle just inside negative territory, supported by strong domestic demand.
An analyst said that the June interest rate future risked a "pretty strong correction" on Monday if the left wins Sunday's run-off vote.
A Reuter survey conducted on Thursday said a victory by the left would knock another 30 basis points of the June PIBOR interest rate contract.

French 10-year bonds were yielding 10 points less than German paper, against nine points on Wednesday. The franc traded at 3.3788 against the mark, up from Wednesday's 3.3816 but still below its pre-election level of around 3.36 per mark.
Bond traders said they believed that whatever the outcome of the Sunday election, France's position towards European Monetary Union (EMU) would be largely the same.

"During an election campaign, people focus on the normal right-left debate, but all politicians who get close to power are caught into a funnel which takes them towards the single currency. Nobody dares to torpedo that," a trader said.
French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin told the Le Monde newspaper on Thursday that his party backed Europe's planned single currency and that this would be the position of a left-wing government.
"We are for the single currency, since the ouset. One can be against the single currency and that's a respectable stance but it would not be the position of a government," he said.
